project: quay-krewe: a project carries its own context
rewritten: 2026-09-04, a fourth time, after the design settled the operator's own commands

user_actions.1: A project holds a brief and a design, and any write to the design clears the approval.
user_actions.2: The design carries a numbered path of atomised changes.
user_actions.3: The operator takes a step, and the session proves it understood before it builds. Several steps run at once, up to the project's cap, and a take is refused when two steps name the same file.
user_actions.4: The operator approves a restatement, and the session builds.
user_actions.5: The operator reads the state of the path.
user_actions.6: Krewe checks the proof, and a step records what came of it.
user_actions.7: Krewe earns the word done, and can lose it.
user_actions.8: The operator drives krewe from a slash command in their own session. Krewe writes those command files, and an install never writes over a file somebody else wrote.

rules: One intention per slice. One reviewable pull request per slice. Revertable alone.
Every slice ships its scenarios in the same change. The promises gate refuses a behaviour change that carries no scenario.
Each slice is written for somebody who was not in the design conversation.
S-5 is the gate. If the measurement says no, every slice after it is cancelled.

The whole suite runs on this machine and in continuous integration. It takes about 42 seconds and peaks at about 1.18 gigabytes. The local gates are make test, go build, go vet, gofmt and golangci-lint.
Each slice names the milestone of .greenlight/ROADMAP.md it belongs to. Sixteen milestones, thirty five slices, because a milestone that is more than one reviewable pull request is split.

The dependency edges order by meaning, not by file. Section 5.1 of the design measures what that does not record. From milestone 7 on, several steps may be taken at once, capped at three by default, and every take is a command the operator typed.

slices.name: A skill teaches a session to design a project
slices.intention: Let an ordinary session carry the ideation and the design, with no machinery around it.
slices.changes: One skill, prose only, no code. It tells a session to read the brief and the repository, and then to write the design. It tells it to write the path in the grammar, and to name a scenario on every step. It tells it never to approve. It states the six parts of a restatement.
slices.proves: features/design.feature. A session dispatched with the skill writes a design and a path that read back whole. Every step names a scenario. The design it wrote is not approved.
slices.note: This is the headline capability and it rests on everything above it. The session stays ordinary and is dispatched by hand. No controller and no gate on it.

slices.name: The console draws a project's path
slices.intention: Let the operator read the path without leaving the console.
slices.changes: A path resource, drilled into from a project. Columns: number, title, state, proof, closed by, session, age. A step that waits for the operator draws waiting on you. Enter descends into the project's sessions when the step names one.
slices.proves: internal/console table tests for the columns, the order, the derived cell and the refusal. features/console.feature for the view opening by name.
slices.note: SortBy is -1. The control plane answers in number order, and sorting rendered text would put step 10 above step 2. It depends on S-25 because the closer cell reads a column that migration 0069 adds.

slices.name: The project row counts the steps, the trust level and the flight
slices.intention: Say how far a project got, and where krewe stands, on the listing an operator already reads.
slices.changes: The projects view gains two cells. One counts done steps out of total. The other shows the trust level with the run behind it, and says when an offer stands. One ListSteps call per draw, not one per project.
slices.proves: internal/console table tests. A project with seven steps, three done, draws 3/7. A project with no path draws an empty cell. A project at level 0 with two agreements draws 0 (2/5). A project with a standing offer says so.
slices.note: Project gains no field on the wire. Both cells are derived by the reader.

slices.name: Krewe installs the slash commands, and the init command ships
slices.intention: Put krewe in the operator's own terminal, and prove an install never writes over somebody else's file.

partial_contracts.SLASH-1: The embed, the marker and the file format. The set holds one file here, and grows to four.
partial_contracts.SLASH-3: Whole, as a test over the embedded set. It runs again on every file a later slice adds.
partial_contracts.COMMAND-23: The listing. It names one command here, and four after S-35.

slices.changes: A new commands directory carrying one markdown file. A new internal package holding the embed and the install. The words krewe commands, krewe commands install and krewe commands list. Nothing touches the store.
slices.proves: features/commands.feature. An install writes every file and names where each went. A second install replaces the files krewe wrote. An install over a file with no marker refuses, names it, and writes nothing at all. Every embedded file carries the marker on line one. Every verb the files name appears in the manual.
slices.gate: There is no flag that forces a write over an unmarked file. One scenario reads the flag table and proves none exists.
slices.why_here: The install mechanism alone could ship after S-3. It waits because milestone 15 ships the design command beside it, and that command dispatches a session holding the skill of S-29.
slices.note: No migration, no table, no protobuf message and no remote procedure call. A reader who expects one should stop looking.

slices.name: The design command asks, dispatches, and shows the design back
slices.intention: Let the operator run the whole design conversation from their own terminal.
slices.changes: One markdown file. It asks the design questions in the operator's session. It then dispatches a krewe session that holds the design skill. It reads the body back with krewe design, and runs krewe design approve on a yes.
slices.proves: features/commands.feature. The file installs and carries the marker. It names only verbs the manual carries. It writes no design body itself. Answering no leaves the design unapproved.
slices.risk: This is the command where breaking the rule of SLASH-3 would be easiest. A scenario reads the file and refuses a design body written in the operator's session.
slices.note: The design work stays in a krewe session in a sandbox, where the record keeps it.

slices.name: The status command prints one readout of the path
slices.intention: Give the operator the whole state of a project in one line of typing.
slices.changes: One markdown file. It runs krewe path, krewe sessions and krewe design. It prints the steps in flight against the cap, what waits on the operator, the next step and the trust level.
slices.proves: features/commands.feature. The file installs and carries the marker. It names only verbs the manual carries. A project with two steps in flight and a cap of three reads back as such. A project with no path names the command that writes one.
slices.why_here: It reads the cap from S-14, the next step from S-13 and the trust level from S-25. All three are ancestors of S-32, so the only edge it needs is the install.
slices.note: It writes nothing. Every number in the readout comes from a row somebody else wrote.

slices.name: The trust command prints the ladder and raises it on a yes
slices.intention: Put the offer in front of the operator where they already stand.

partial_contracts.COMMAND-23: The listing now names four commands, in the order init, design, status, trust.

slices.changes: One markdown file. It runs krewe trust, prints the level, the run, the threshold and any standing offer, and runs krewe trust raise on a yes. The listing now names four commands.
slices.proves: features/commands.feature. The file installs and carries the marker. With an offer standing, a yes raises the level and krewe trust then says level 1. With no offer it prints the run and asks nothing. Answering no leaves the level where it was.
slices.note: It never lowers a level. A wrong close does that, through krewe step reopen.
